stem: A set of ancient Indian mental-calculation techniques (based on 16 sutras attributed to Bharati Krishna Tirthaji), used to teach students fast multiplication, squaring, and division shortcuts, is popularly known as:
explanation: Vedic Mathematics offers rapid mental-calculation shortcuts using sutras (formulae) — a supplementary technique for speed and number sense, distinct from the Heuristic Method (guided self-discovery of a solution procedure) or the Laboratory Method (hands-on activity-based verification).

subject: Mathematics
stem: A teacher explicitly connects a mathematics lesson on percentages to a Social Studies lesson on population growth and a Science lesson on concentration of solutions, showing students how the same mathematical idea applies across subjects. This pedagogical principle, one of the core maxims of teaching mathematics, is called the maxim of:
explanation: The maxim of Correlation links mathematics with other school subjects (and with real life) to show its practical relevance and reinforce learning — distinct from maxims describing the internal sequencing of a single lesson, like simple-to-complex or known-to-unknown.
